name: What is a floor plan reconfiguration, and how does it differ from standard remodeling?

mainEntity.name: What is a floor plan reconfiguration, and how does it differ from standard remodeling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Floor plan reconfiguration involves modifying the internal layout of your home by moving, removing, or adding walls. Unlike a standard cosmetic renovation that simply swaps out cabinets or fixtures, this work alters the flow, traffic patterns, and spatial relationships between rooms. Common examples include open-concept conversions between the kitchen and living room, combining small bedrooms, or shifting hallway boundaries to enlarge a primary bathroom suite. Because it changes the structural or mechanical organization of the home, this service typically requires structural engineering assessments, electrical rerouting, and city building permits before construction begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: A floor plan reconfiguration rearranges walls and internal room layouts to change flow and space, whereas standard remodeling simply updates fixtures and finishes within existing boundaries.
